Glib

GLIB -- probably from a Germanic root related to 'slippery.' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Glib is speaking smoothly and fluently, but in a way that seems superficial or insincere.

Around the office, he was famous for having a glib comeback ready for literally any complaint, no matter how serious.

Worked Example

Whenever a customer complained, the salesman had a glib response ready in an instant -- smooth, quick, and never quite addressing the actual problem.

Notice glib is about HOW someone talks -- a fast, smooth, effortless delivery that feels shallow or insincere -- rather than about whether a specific claim or argument is logically sound (that's Specious).

Build the Word

The pieces

root — glib-

root — glib-: slippery, smooth (probably Germanic or Low German)

Put it together

Put it together: Glib most likely comes from an old Germanic word for 'slippery.' That image fits perfectly: glib talk slides right past you, sounding smooth and quick, without ever quite catching on anything solid or sincere.

Use the root in a new word: glibly

Use the root in a new word: glibly: He glibly promised the investors a full refund, knowing perfectly well the company had no money left.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Glib describes a MANNER of speaking -- smooth, fast, superficially confident, but insincere. Compare Specious, which describes whether an ARGUMENT or claim actually holds up logically. A glib speaker can state a specious argument, but the two words describe different things: Glib is about style, Specious is about substance.
